newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Power shortfall worries Bangladesh private sector.
newsitem.headline: Power shortfall worries Bangladesh private sector.

text.p: Bangladesh's top business leader on Saturday expressed serious concern at the crippling electricity shortfall, saying frequent power cuts had threatened economic activities.

"Production and exports are worst hit by frequent power cuts. I am receiving eight to 10 complaints every day from southeastern Chittagong industrial belt alone," Yusuf Abdullah Harun, Chief of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), told a news conference in Dhaka.
He said the government must tackle the power problem with urgent attention. Bangladesh was now producing 1,700 megawatts of electricity against a minimum requirement of 2,200 MW.

Energy Ministry officials said there was no immediate chance of any significant improvement in power generation, though the government was planning to set up three barge-mounted power plants which would produce 300 MW by December.
Harun said Bangladesh's poor infrastructure which was discouraging local and foreign investment.

He also called for immediate steps on privatisation of public enterprises which, he said, were using up more than two percent of Bangladesh's GDP in subsidies and restricting the government's spending on infrastructure development.
Public enterprises in Bangladesh claim about 25 billion taka ($600 million) annually in subsidies from the exchequer.
